key_insight: The best universal ML interatomic potential matches AFLOW formation energies about as closely as another DFT database does, making reference controls essential to trustworthy rankings.
engineering_relevance: Alloy-screening workflows should check elemental references and cross-database DFT disagreement before interpreting energy or stability errors as model failures.
method: Benchmark 14 universal ML interatomic potentials on 1.45 million ordered intermetallics against AFLOW, which none used for training.
Compare energy and stability errors with disagreement among AFLOW, Alexandria, and OQMD.
Re-reference energies and screen broken elemental references to test ranking robustness.
evidence_signal: DFT databases differ by less than 6–8 meV/atom for half the structures but average 16–30 meV/atom disagreement; after re-referencing, the next four models sit 2–7 meV/atom above the reference-disagreement floor.
watch_item: Reference disagreement limits interpretable benchmark accuracy, and these ordered-intermetallic results do not establish performance across all alloy properties or configurations.
paper_title: How good are universal MLIPs for alloys? A benchmark is only as trustworthy as its controls
